title: Foreign countries recruiting nurses should also support Ghana’s health system
summary: A September 2026 GNA report covered calls for international recruitment arrangements to include support for Ghana’s health system, including workforce development and training.
body: A September 2, 2026 report from the Ghana News Agency covered a call for destination countries recruiting Ghanaian nurses and midwives to contribute to strengthening the health system that trained them.
The report described international mobility as a legitimate career option while also discussing staffing pressures and the need for fair, ethical and sustainable workforce arrangements.

For users of the Hub, the practical point is to separate a news announcement from an individual application decision. A vacancy still needs employer verification, regulator requirements, eligibility checks, closing dates and any sponsorship wording.
The Hub therefore presents this as an internal explainer and links the relevant country pathway to its own evaluation workflow.

title: Ghana Immigration Service warns the public about fake overseas job offers
summary: A Ghana News Agency report said the Ghana Immigration Service cautioned prospective migrants to verify job offers and recruitment agencies before paying money or travelling.
body: On August 28, 2026, the Ghana News Agency reported a warning from the Ghana Immigration Service about fraudulent overseas job offers and recruitment schemes.
The report urged prospective migrants to verify recruitment agencies and job offers before making payments or travelling, noting the risk of exploitation and trafficking.

The Hub reflects this warning in its job workflow: listings display source and verification information, and the actual official application route is not exposed as a general clickable job link before the relevant pathway review.
Users should be cautious about anyone asking for money through informal channels in exchange for a job or visa promise.

title: Capacity-building programme trains 40 health professionals in the Ashanti Region
summary: A September 4 GNA report described a two-day training programme for 40 health professionals, including midwives and physician assistants, focused on strengthening healthcare delivery.
body: GNA reported on September 4, 2026 that a two-day capacity-building programme in the Ashanti Region brought together 40 health professionals.
The report said the programme particularly supported specialised health professionals such as midwives and physician assistants and focused on improving service quality, efficiency and accessibility.
For students and professionals, the story reinforces the role of continuing skills development alongside formal qualifications and registration.
The Hub can use this type of update as a prompt for users to review the Professional Practice modules, CPD-oriented resources and career-planning tools.

title: Ghana sends first batch of 121 health professionals to Antigua
summary: The Presidency reported that 121 nurses, midwives and allied health professionals were sent to Antigua under the Ghana Labour Exchange Programme.
body: The Presidency reported on January 27, 2026 that Ghana had sent a first group of 121 nurses, midwives and other allied health professionals to Antigua under the Ghana Labour Exchange Programme.

The announcement described the arrangement as part of bilateral cooperation intended to create employment and professional-development opportunities and address a backlog of qualified unemployed health professionals.

A government-to-government mobility programme is different from a normal open job advertisement. The conditions, selection process, documentation and timing must be taken from the programme’s official notices.
The Hub keeps this announcement as policy and mobility news rather than presenting it as a current vacancy.

title: Ghana–Jamaica health workforce arrangement creates a structured mobility route
summary: GNA reported on a bilateral health workforce arrangement involving credential verification, licensing, deployment and orientation between Ghana and Jamaica.
body: GNA reported on May 27, 2026 that Ghana and Jamaica had entered a bilateral health workforce arrangement covering the movement of qualified health professionals.
The report described operational areas such as credential verification, professional licensing, deployment, orientation and welfare support.
The practical message for applicants is that an agreement does not automatically qualify every applicant for every role. Individual professional and immigration requirements continue to matter.
The Ministry of Health recruitment portal is retained in the Hub as an official Ghana source for any future programme notices.

title: WHO: the global nursing and midwifery workforce continues to face uneven distribution
summary: WHO’s August 2026 nursing and midwifery fact sheet highlights workforce growth alongside persistent shortages, uneven distribution and international migration.
body: The World Health Organization’s August 11, 2026 fact sheet reported that the global nursing workforce had grown, while significant shortages and unequal distribution remained.
WHO also reported a large global midwifery gap and emphasized education, employment, regulation, leadership and working conditions as important parts of workforce planning.
The publication also places international recruitment within the broader need for ethical workforce migration and cooperation between source and destination countries.
The Hub uses this information to provide context for users considering international career pathways.

title: N&MC licensing examinations cover multiple nurse and midwife cadres
source: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Ghana
summary: The N&MC publishes current licensing examination and registration information for multiple nursing and midwifery cadres.
body: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Ghana states that it conducts licensing examinations for Nurse Assistants, Nurses and Midwives.
The Council lists several examination cadres, including Registered General Nurses, Registered Midwives, Registered Community Nurses, Registered Mental Nurses and a range of post-basic programmes.
The Hub’s preparation bank is separate original study material. It is designed to help users practise knowledge and clinical reasoning without claiming to reproduce official examination papers.
For current examination schedules, eligibility, registration and official procedures, the Council’s current publications remain the authoritative source.

title: Recent reporting highlights nursing workforce pressure in a regional referral hospital
summary: Recent GNA reporting described staffing pressure across nursing and midwifery units at a regional referral facility and linked the issue to broader workforce challenges.
body: A recent Ghana News Agency report examined nursing and midwifery staffing pressure at a regional referral hospital, describing shortages in several clinical units.
The report is relevant to professional discussions about staffing, further training, workforce planning and the effect of personnel availability on service delivery.
The story is presented as a news explainer rather than a clinical directive. Users should consult their employers and official health authorities for operational information.
For students, the topic connects to health-system management, leadership, community health and professional-practice study.
